subject: Stress windows, throttle ceilings, and failover — Redwood vs Hyperscalers (post-demo)
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Ellie Tan <ellie.tan@clearpath.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Stress windows, throttle ceilings, and failover — Redwood vs Hyperscalers (post-demo)

Hi Ellie —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we keep momentum: we focused on three areas you asked us to validate:

1) Reliability/SLOs: uptime targets, error budgets, and failover behavior across regions.
2) Throttling and rate limits: steady-state ceilings and behavior under sudden spikes (burst vs sustained).
3) Comparative behavior vs hyperscaler-managed endpoints (in particular the behavior when a primary region is degraded).

What we observed together: Redwood’s continuous batching + prefix caching reduced median tail latency during the 1–2 minute demo spike noticeably vs the sample hyperscaler run we showed. We also demonstrated the automatic fallback route to the warm standby model variant which prevents soft failures when the primary hits ephemeral resource pressure.

Proposed next tests (we can own these and run with your test harness, or you can run them against our hosted endpoints):
- Spike window test: 5k concurrent short requests for 3 x 60s windows (measure p50/p95/p99 latencies and failure rate).
- Throttle ceiling test: ramp to sustained 500 rps for 30m and observe throttling mode and error-rate evolution.
- Failover runbook test: simulate region N+1 outage and validate routing + warm-standby latency impact and cold-start behavior.
- Error budget verification: exercise our SLOs against your incident injection schedule and produce an error-budget burn report.

Deliverables we’ll send in next 48 hours: the demo recording, a short runbook for each test, and a proposed mutual action plan with owners and dates. Also attaching a concise capabilities brief that maps each test to the telemetry we’ll produce (token-level traces, per-route drop counts, and KV-cache hit rates).

Next immediate asks for you: share the test harness (endpoint URLs, auth token, and any IP allowlist windows) and confirm whether procurement should be looped in now or after the first round of testing.

Attachments: redwood-demo-recording-20270715.mp4 (recording link), redwood-capabilities-brief.pdf (one-pager).

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-min follow-up if that helps (I blocked 2–4pm PT tomorrow but am flexible).

—
Logan Wright
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0172

From: Ellie Tan <ellie.tan@clearpath.ai>

Subject: Re: Stress windows, throttle ceilings, and failover — Redwood vs Hyperscalers (post-demo)

Thanks Logan — great walkthrough. Couple quick notes from our side: we liked how the warm-standby cut the tail in the demo.

We can run the spike/ceiling tests ourselves in our staging harness (we prefer to own the traffic generator), but we’ll need a stable test credential and a short runbook from you for the expected telemetry fields. I attached our security questionnaire and the procurement contact (procurement@clearpath.ai) in case we need to begin T&Cs for a pilot.

Quick answers:
- We can schedule the first test block next Wednesday (21 Jul) between 07:00–11:00 PT.
- We will share IP allowlist details by Monday and will need the endpoint be accessible from our staging VPC.
- Procurement would like a one-page pilot quote after the first successful test block.

Thanks again — looping procurement in the next message.

Best,
Ellie
Director of Platform, ClearPath AI
ellie.tan@clearpath.ai

Attachment: clearpath-security-questions.xlsx

Ben / Marissa —

Ellie wants to run the first staging block on Wed 21 Jul 07:00–11:00 PT from their harness. Action items:

- Ben: prep a short runbook + sample telemetry JSON schema by EOD Monday (include token-level latency traces, cache hit metric, per-route drop counts). Also include the auth token lifecycle rules and IP allowlist steps.
- Marissa: I’ll need a one-page pilot quote (30-day pilot, up to 500k tokens, support response SLA) for procurement to review. Please flag any pricing floors or approval needs.
- Ops: coordinate a warm standby seed to ensure the failover run shows only minimal cold-start variance; we should run a short internal smoke test Tue afternoon to validate seeding.

I’m offering to host the endpoint from our hosted stack so we can capture the full telemetry; if ClearPath insists on their staging, Ben please document the pattern for request headers we expect so their harness can annotate traces.

I’ll loop procurement once Marissa shares the pilot quote.

—
Logan
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 18 Jul 2027 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FW: Stress windows, throttle ceilings, and failover — Redwood vs Hyperscalers (post-demo)

Ack — I’ll get the runbook + telemetry schema over by EOD Monday (sending from my account so we have a single-source doc). Couple clarifications I want to capture in the runbook:

- For the spike test please confirm request size distribution (most of ClearPath’s calls are short payloads ~120–220 tokens). I’ll include both short and mixed payload profiles.
- Throttle ceiling: Redwood will respond with 429s once the per-API-route concurrency cap is exceeded; we’ll also include a backoff guidance table and expected retry windows.
- Failover: we’ll document expected warm-standby latency delta (p95 + expected cache-warmup window) and a short checklist for stateful resources that might need reseeding.

I’ll attach the runbook to the hubspot action item and cc you both.

—Ben
